title: Review of c42's dt/2 check of the food chain: on new seed 7 at the world's own dt=0.25, prey and predators still both divide and coexist (prey 21 persistent splits, generation 5; predators 32, generation 2)
summary: The claim's world.py with WORLD_P {"dt":0.25} (the world's integration step; --spf 400 keeps 100 t per frame), seed 7, 128^2, t=12000, --lineage-k 5. Prey: 21 persistent splits, max generation 5, merge/split 0.09, 16 at the end; predators: 32 persistent splits, generation 2, merge/split 0.24, 27 at the end. My dt=0.5 run of the same seed (20261026T1600-c44-review-foodchain): prey 15 (generation 4), predators 30 (generation 3). Same picture as the finding: coexistence and both kinds dividing do not depend on the step; split counts move by tens of percent.

observations.D: rerun/dthalf/seed7/FACTS.md species blocks: prey 21 persistent splits (generation 5), predators 32 (generation 2) at dt 0.25, against 15 (generation 4) and 30 (generation 3) at dt 0.5 on the same seed; sheet shows prey dumbbells and predator rings/arcs throughout

seeds_run.result: pass: both kinds divide and coexist at dt 0.25

verdicts.limitation: One new seed; lineage window 500 t (K=5) as in the claim; no grid-spacing variant. labkit's FACTS header reads 'world META dt 0.5' because META is fixed, but step() integrates with P['dt']=0.25.
